articles.headline: Arsenal's Mikel Merino: I am 'fortunate to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack
articles.description: Mikel Merino has revealed that the conversations in the dressing room in the aftermath of Arsenal's draw to Wolves last season was when he realised they would win the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルのミケル・メリノ：ドルトムントのバス襲撃の後、「生きていて幸運だ」
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・メリノは、昨シーズンのアーセナルがウルブスと引き分けた後のロッカールームでの会話が、チームがプレミアリーグで優勝できると確信した瞬間だったと明かした。
articles.body:
Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino has said he is "fortunate to be alive" after switching seats on the Borussia Dortmund team bus that came under attack in 2017. 

Dortmund were on their way to the Westfallenstadion for a Champions League quarterfinal in 2017 when three pipe bombs went off and smashed the windows of their bus. The bus nearly toppled over and while there were no casualties, defender Marc Bartra badly cut his wrist. 

"I think I have an angel on my shoulder. I'm actually fortunate to be alive at all," he said in an interview to The Players Tribune.

"I was 20 and playing for Dortmund when three pipe bombs went off right next to our bus on the way to a Champions League match. A lot of young people probably would not even believe that it happened, or how bad it was, but it marked us all.

"There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up. The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat.

"That day, the seat was empty. My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life.

"So yeah, I just have this belief that things happen for a reason."

The moment he realised Arsenal would win the Premier League

Merino left Dortmund in 2017 and had spells at Newcastle and Real Sociedad before joining Arsenal in 2024. He was part of the side that ended the Gunners' 22-year wait for a league title. 

He revealed that the conversations in the dressing room in the aftermath of Arsenal's draw to Wolves last season was when he realised they would win the Premier League.

While the Gunners eventually finished seven points clear of second-place Manchester City, it was a hard-fought title race in which the Gunners wobbled on a few occassions.

The draw at Molineux in mid-February was one of them. Arsenal were 2-0 up against bottom-side Wolves before throwing away their lead in dramatic fashion. It was the second time in three games they had dropped points and with a trip to local rivals Tottenham to follow, their title push appeared on the brink of collapse.

"To be honest, there were doubts inside the team too," Merino said.

"Giving away a 2-0 lead should never happen. But the day after the game, the players had a meeting inside the dressing room, without the boss. Everyone spoke up. Nobody talked about tactics. This was about how a group of human beings handle adversity together.

"I spoke about how I saw the team from the outside [Merino was injured at the time], and I said that this was something we as players had to handle, because the boss couldn't do everything for us. When one person has so many tasks at one club, you need leaders who can figure things out on their own.

articles.headline: Brazil winger Antony's home burgled during Real Betis Champions League match
articles.description: Brazil winger Antony has revealed that his home in Seville was burgled during Real Betis' Champions League clash against Porto on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: ブラジル人ウィングのアントニー、レアル・ベティスのチャンピオンズリーグ戦中に自宅が空き巣被害
articles.descriptionJa: ブラジル人ウィングのアントニーは、水曜日に行われたレアル・ベティス対ポルトのチャンピオンズリーグ戦の最中に、セビリアにある自宅が空き巣被害に遭ったことを明かした。
articles.body:
Brazil winger Antony has revealed that his home in Seville was burgled while he was playing for Real Betis in their Champions League match against Porto on Wednesday.

The former Manchester United player, who started at the La Cartuja stadium, posted a statement on his Instagram story: "A night that promised to be brilliant ended up becoming a night of anger, sadness, and frustration. My home was burgled."

"Knowing that everything we have achieved with so much effort, work and dedication has been taken by someone who has no idea of ​​the battles that we have had to fight to achieve each thing.

"What angers me most is not just the material loss, but the feeling of insecurity inside the place where we should feel most protected.

"It's looking at my family and seeing, in the eyes of the people I love most, the fear and insecurity that a situation like this leaves in its wake. There is no material possession in the world more valuable than my family's life and well-being."

 Antony is the second LaLiga player to report a home robbery this week.

Villarreal goalkeeper Péter Gulácsi sat out his team's Champions League win over Napoli on Tuesday after he and his family were victims of an armed robbery a day earlier.

Gulacsi, who returned to training on Thursday, said no one was injured but described the ordeal as "deeply traumatic."

Antony joined Betis initially on loan in January 2025 before making his transfer permanent later that summer.

articles.headline: James Maddison can be the difference maker for Tottenham - former Coventry academy coach
articles.description: James Maddison has been backed to be the missing piece of the puzzle for Tottenham by old Coventry academy coach Richard Stevens.
articles.headlineJa: ジェームズ・マディソンはトッテナムの勝敗を分ける存在になり得る ― 元コベントリーのアカデミーコーチ
articles.descriptionJa: 元コベントリーのアカデミーコーチであるリチャード・スティーブンスは、ジェームズ・マディソンがトッテナムにとってパズルの欠けていた最後のピースになると支持している。
articles.body:
James Maddison has been backed to be the missing piece of the puzzle for Tottenham by old Coventry academy coach Richard Stevens.

Spurs remain winless in the Premier League after six matches, but produced an impressive display in Saturday's 1-1 draw at Manchester United -- where Maddison came off the bench for a fifth time this season.

The 29-year-old has struggled to get back to full fitness after two serious knee injuries in 2025, including a rupture of his anterior cruciate ligament, but Stevens, who was academy manager during Maddison's time at Sky Blues, believes the playmaker can become Tottenham's difference maker again.

Ahead of Coventry's trip to Spurs on Monday, Stevens told the Press Association: "His driver is, 'Am I playing 90 minutes and can I go and score some goals and ignite the fans,' you know? So this injury would have hurt him a lot.

"Even in a 10-minute spell [now,] when he comes on, he takes the ball and he makes things happen.

"He makes things tick and he gets the team playing forwards. He gets the team moving up the pitch.

"And good grief, Tottenham have had a tough time. They're an unbelievable football club and you know the players they have, maybe he's the bit that's going to connect everything together.

"I hope he's going to return and he's going to connect everything together for Tottenham because I think he has that ability to do that."

Stevens watched 52 youth prospects make their full debut for Coventry during 12 years in charge of the academy and can remember how a young Maddison "ran that group" to ensure certain standards were met.

Coventry's financial plight more than a decade ago opened the door to youth-teamers and despite being sent off in his 12th appearance, Maddison grasped his chance and scored in a final day win at Crawley which kept his boyhood club in League One.

Four years later and he had played for England.

Tottenham were interested in Maddison in 2016, but had to wait another seven years to secure his services and a rollercoaster spell in N17 has followed of 83 appearances, one Europa League triumph and a nervy relegation battle.

Ahead of Maddison's third meeting with Coventry, Stevens can still recall the diminutive midfielder that caught the eye on his first day.

"James was Under-11. We were away at MK Dons and there was this pitch behind me and there's this little fella who just kind of carried the ball and twisted and turned," Stevens said.

"We knew he was a good player. Every team we ever played against were always aware of him and they knew him. And, I've said it many times, he just loved football.

"Loved football, obsessed with it and no surprise he has had the career he's had.

"If you see those pictures of that 2014-15 season, he does look like a boy, but he might have been a boy in his body, but he certainly wasn't a boy in his mentality, in his understanding of the game and his courage.

articles.headline: Trey Nyoni backed by Liverpool's Andoni Iraola amid midfield injury issues
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has every faith in Trey Nyoni as the 19-year-old looks set for his first Premier League start.
articles.headlineJa: 中盤の負傷者問題が続く中、リヴァプールのアンドニ・イラオラがトレイ・ニョニを支持
articles.descriptionJa: 19歳のトレイ・ニョニがプレミアリーグ初先発を果たす見込みとなる中、リヴァプールのアンドニ・イラオラ監督は彼に全幅の信頼を寄せている。
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has every faith in Trey Nyoni as the 19-year-old looks set for his first Premier League start.

The teenager put in a composed display in the 6-3 Champions League win over LASK in midweek, and with Ryan Gravenberch suspended and Dominik Szoboszlai still struggling with a hamstring injury, it is likely he will line up alongside Alexis Mac Allister at Brentford.

Nyoni has made a total of 26 appearances since his debut in February 2024, 10 of which have been as a substitute in the top flight, but after playing 85 minutes on his first Champions League start in the midweek win over LASK, Iraola has no doubts about the youngster's quality.

"Trey is a player that I think is very young with not a lot of minutes in the first team, but is very mature, he understands the situation very well, he understands the game very well and tactically he is very smart," said the Basque.

"But he has to continue doing the steps in the right direction, I am confident with him.

"He has been involved in most of the last games but he has to keep this level of performance, of training, he has to play as a six, as an eight, he has to play one minute, he has to start and play a game like LASK, putting pressure on the other midfielders.

"It is very good for us that we can put in these young players with not a lot of experience and they can perform in a competition like the Champions League or the Premier League."

Liverpool are currently in a run of six games in 18 days and so Iraola knows he will have to call on Nyoni regularly.

"In this period, especially, where we are basically playing every three days, less than three days, you need more players," he said.

"That's why we changed the team [midweek] and we need to change again at the weekend and change again when we face Villarreal in another three days.

"We will need everyone in one moment or another, everyone has to be ready because we will need him probably.

"But this is the challenge of playing, no? It's competitions like the Champions League and it's not going to just happen this week, it is going to be a constant thing this season so we have to adapt.

"We have to be ready. The same way it was a quick turnaround after Manchester City, this is going to be a quick one, the next one, we have like four that are just two days in between games. That is not normal but has happened this time and we have to adapt to these circumstances.

"I expect everyone to be at their best mentally and physically because, Brentford, you cannot play comfortable against them, we know this, so we have to be ready for a battle."

articles.headline: Manchester City charges: Features, explainers, what's next after guilty verdict
articles.description: ESPN has you covered with everything you need to know about the latest in the Manchester City scandal.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティの疑惑：特集、解説、有罪判決後の展望
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのスキャンダルに関する最新情報について、ESPNが知っておくべきすべてを網羅してお伝えします。
articles.body:
After an investigation spanning years, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. The decision is a major development in one of the biggest scandals in soccer history, but the saga is far from over.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

Tighe: Man City's alternate universe: Guardiola, Haaland to Arsenal? Arteta to PSG?

What would the sport have looked like if City had not spent in the way that they did? Who would have won the eight league titles? Where would the superstars (like Erling Haaland) they signed have gone instead? And what would manager Pep Guardiola's career have looked like without a decade-long stint in Manchester?

Lindop: Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

Under Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola, Liverpool and Man City pushed the Premier League's standards higher than ever. But was it all a sham?

Dawson: 'We're Not Really Here': As Man City sanctions loom, it's the fans who suffer

Manchester City's financial malfeasance could send the club back down the football pyramid, a place where fans of a certain age are very familiar.

Olley: Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict

Does Arsenal's comeback win over Leeds close the gap on leaders Man City, or extend their own lead at the top? This is the perpetual uncertainty that hangs over the Premier League now.

Ogden: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?

Marcotti: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero

It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

O'Hanlon: Mock draft: How would Premier League teams pick if Man City cheating scandal took a turn?

Now that Manchester City have been found to have cheated on a huge scale, anything is on the table -- maybe even an American-style Premier League draft?

Multiple contributors: How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict

Four clubs (Arsenal, Liverpool, Man United and Tottenham) retained their legal rights in the Premier League's case against Man City. Now that a guilty verdict has been issued, what will they do in response?

articles.headline: Premier League Top 50: Ranking the best players so far this season
articles.description: The Premier League Top 50 returns for the 2026-27 season to rank the best players across the league so far.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ・トップ50：今シーズンこれまでのベストプレーヤーをランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 「プレミアリーグ・トップ50」が2026-27シーズンに復活。リーグ全体でこれまでに活躍した最高の選手たちをランキング化します。
articles.body:
Let's dig into the big question that's on everybody's mind: Who, uh, is the best player in the Premier League?

While we wait for the league to issue its punishment to Manchester City for breaking 114 rules and cheating their way to a spend of $1 billion more than regulations allowed, the games still go on.

Did you know Jordan Henderson scored twice last week? For Chelsea? Also: None of the promoted teams are in the relegation zone! Hull City are tied for seventh! Everton ... are tied for fourth?

To take stock of what has suddenly become -- and will continue to be -- the weirdest Premier League season of all time, we've decided to roll out the second edition of ESPN's Premier League Top 50, with our first coming before the season began.

We'll ask it again: Who is the best player in the Premier League? And now we'll answer it.

How we rank the players and who missed out

As we've done for the past two years, the rankings are meant to be a combination of true talent, how much value a player has actually provided and how much better that player is than the average players at his position.

The list is still tilted toward goal-producing-and-creating players on the best teams in England, but it opens up space for defenders and midfielders and goalkeepers from a bunch of different places up and down the table.

Injured players are ineligible, so you won't see the likes of Arsenal's William Saliba, Liverpool's Hugo Ekitike or Bournemouth's Alex Scott on the list.

You also won't see Liverpool's Bradley Barcola, who I'd expect to be on the list by the end of the season, but who has had almost no impact on any of the Premier League matches he has played thus far. A couple of other new signings -- Barcola's club and country teammate Jérémy Jacquet and Aston Villa's record signing Johan Manzambi -- have already broken into the top 50 with impressive starts to their Premier League careers.

Unless otherwise noted, most of the data you'll see throughout the piece comes from the stats app Futi. OK, let's get to the top 50...

There's a great new book by David Epstein called "Inside the Box." It's, essentially, about how we tend to be at our best -- whether on our own or as groups -- where we're forced into constraints.

There are infinitely more options at our disposal today compared with 30 years ago; constraints help with that problem. But they also seem to make us more creative, more productive and happier.

See: Everton Football Club. Last summer they signed a promising young striker from Villarreal with a nice track record of getting lots of high-quality shots. But he was mostly a backup behind the veteran Beto, who left this offseason.

Everton tried to sign U.S. men's national team standout Folarin Balogun on the final day of the transfer window -- only for it to fall apart because of issues Everton had with Balogun's medical clearance exam.

articles.headline: Defense bails out Broncos in OT win as Nix, offense struggle
articles.description: The Broncos' D came up with five sacks, 17 QB hits and two interceptions, enabling Denver to win even though the offense finished with only 168 net yards.
articles.headlineJa: 守備陣がブロンコスの延長戦勝利を救う、ニックスと攻撃陣は苦戦
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスの守備陣は5つのサック、17回のQBヒット、2つのインターセプトを記録。攻撃陣の獲得総ヤードがわずか168ヤードに留まったものの、デンバーを勝利に導きました。
articles.body:
DENVER -- With a 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks finally in hand, Denver Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto was still trying to wrap his head around one of the numbers that told the story of the night.

The Broncos (4-2) had survived, somehow, despite the fact that the team's defense faced 82 snaps Thursday night in Empower Field at Mile High, just four days after a road win at the Los Angeles Chargers.

"82 snaps? Did I feel 82 snaps? Bro, every one of them," Bonitto said with a tired smile.

The Broncos' defense sacked Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold five times, hit him 17 times and intercepted him twice, including once in overtime to set up Wil Lutz's 53-yard winning field goal with 4 minutes, 53 seconds left. It all enabled the Broncos to win even though Denver's offense finished with only 168 net yards and didn't have a drive longer than five plays on its last nine possessions of regulation.

The Broncos, without injured Pat Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, still had 12 different players hit Darnold at least once, believed by the team to be the most in an NFL game since at least 2006. It also was the second time this season the Broncos' defense had faced 82 plays (the Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Rams was the other) but this time it was on a short week.

"Defensively we were magnificent,'' Broncos coach Sean Payton said. "I don't know how many times we hit the quarterback, we got three takeaways. ... The takeaways were huge ... that was the difference, field position, all of that. They were fantastic.''

Said Broncos linebacker Justin Strnad: "We pride ourselves on being a dominant unit and we felt like we were that tonight. We knew we were going to get after [Darnold], that was part of the plan and we did that.''

The night didn't have that kind of start. The Broncos' offense put together two long scoring drives in their first three possessions, a season-most 16-play, 74-yard touchdown drive, followed by a nine-play, 79-yard touchdown drive that gave Denver a 14-3 lead.

But in the nine Denver possessions between the second touchdown and Lutz's overtime kick, the offense punted seven times, had a drive go for minus-5 yards to end the half and ended regulation with a possession for a 1-yard loss. The Broncos didn't run more than five plays on any of those possessions, and that put the defense back on the field over and over again without much recovery time.

"We don't win that game without them,'' Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said of the defense.

"We kind of knew it was going to be that kind of game; obviously we want the offense to get rolling a little bit and figure that out,'' Strnad said. "But we're going to do absolutely anything we can to keep winning week in, week out.''

The Broncos had only one game all of last season in which the defense played more than 80 snaps -- 85 against the Washington Commanders last Nov. 30 -- and had only two games in all of 2024 in which the defense played more than 75 snaps.

articles.headline: Seahawks' Sam Darnold owns up to late interceptions in overtime loss to Broncos
articles.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold called his two late interceptions Thursday night "unacceptable" and vowed to be better after a 17-14 loss to the Broncos.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのサム・ダーノルド、ブロンコスに延長戦で敗れ終盤のインターセプトを猛省
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのクォーターバック、サム・ダーノルドは、木曜夜のブロンコス戦での17-14の敗戦後、終盤に投じた2つのインターセプトを「受け入れがたいものだった」とし、改善を誓いました。
articles.body:
DENVER -- Sam Darnold was in position to pull off a comeback win Thursday night, having rallied the Seattle Seahawks from a 14-3 deficit in the fourth quarter after 45 minutes of offensive ineptitude.

Then he threw an interception.

And another one.

Darnold's picks late in regulation and in overtime doomed the Seahawks in a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. It spoiled a brilliant performance from Seattle's defense and dropped the reigning Super Bowl champions to 3-3, putting them 2.5 games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West standings.

"No way to sugarcoat it," Darnold said. "That one sucked. Can't turn the ball over. That's obviously at the forefront of my mind, but there's just a lot that we can do better."

While Darnold was hardly the only one responsible for one of Seattle's more agonizing offensive performances in recent memory, he has thrown seven interceptions in four games since returning from a glute injury in Week 3. He has just as many touchdown passes in that span, and he entered Week 6 ranked 29th in Total QBR (34.4).

"I just think it's B.S for me to keep turning the ball over," he told reporters. "It's not fair to our defense, it's not fair to out special teams group, not fair really to the entire team. So I've got to be better that way."

Darnold made that point to the team in the locker room.

"We have to take care of the ball," coach Mike Macdonald said. "Sam knows that. He told the team that. We've got to take care of the ball."

It's the biggest of several issues that plagued Seattle's offense again Thursday night. The Seahawks managed just 91 yards at halftime with one turnover coming on a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed.

Darnold was sacked five times for the second game in a row, and he took 17 official QB hits. Some of the pressure was the result of breakdowns in pass protection, including free rushers on back-to-back sacks that ended a promising opening drive, while others were a function of Darnold holding onto the ball.

"Our quarterback got hit too much today," Macdonald said. "We've got to do a better job protecting him and we've got to be more decisive with the football. We don't want to take those hits, but they rushed and covered well."

Darnold told offensive coordinator Brian Fleury after Seattle's loss to the 49ers on Sunday that he needed to play more decisively. He felt he did that in the first half against Denver (4-2).

"Dropping back and taking what they give me, I felt like I did a pretty good job of that in the first half," he said. "And then late in the second half, those two plays, just can't have it."

After orchestrating an 11-play, 67-yard drive that resulted in a 1-yard rushing touchdown by George Holani, Darnold hit Shaheed for a 2-point conversion that cut Denver's lead to 14-11 with under six minutes left in regulation.

On the ensuing drive, he was intercepted while trying to hit Tory Horton on third-and-1.

articles.headlineJa: ランゲームと守備がブロンコスを牽引、シアトルに延長戦で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 2つのランニングタッチダウンと5回のサックを記録し、デンバーは「サースデー・ナイト・フットボール」でシアトルを退けた。
articles.body:
DENVER -- In a season in which the Denver Broncos' offense has struggled mightily to construct many scoring drives, let alone big plays, they used just enough small ones to grind out a 17-14 overtime victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night in Empower Field at Mile High.

In coach Sean Payton's second game since he took back playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, the Broncos put together a 16-play drive for their first touchdown of the game -- their longest drive of the season -- to go with a nine-play, 79-yard touchdown for their second one. Denver then survived without another scoring drive.

Payton has preached a need for a reduction in "calories" in the offense as well as more physicality in the run game to make life easier on quarterback Bo Nix. All while the Broncos' defense, which was without All-Pro Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga in the secondary, continued its quarterback-harassing ways. Denver had its second consecutive game with five sacks and an overtime interception from Ja'Quan McMillian.

The Broncos ran it more than they threw it in the Week 5 win against the Los Angeles Chargers and had the scale tipped squarely toward the run game most of the night against the Seahawks -- 26 runs compared to 27 pass attempts before Wil Lutz kicked the winning field goal.

"It's special, that's what we sign up for," Lutz said. "If you don't want that moment, you're not made for it. You kind of saw how the game was unfolding and the chance it was going to come down to the field-goal unit.'"

The victory might not have been suitable for framing, given the Broncos didn't score after the first quarter and had to survive an 11-point fourth quarter from the Seahawks, but it was enough by the wafer-thinnest of margins.

It meant the Broncos have navigated the toughest six-game opening stretch of any team in the league, per ESPN Analytics, with wins against both teams from the NFC Championship Game last season as well as five teams that were in the postseason.

"It was a real challenge for us and I like the way we handled it,'' outside linebacker Nik Bonitto said of the Broncos improving to 4-2.

Here are the most important things to know from Thursday night for both teams:

Denver Broncos (4-2)

Trend to watch: The Broncos, from Payton on down, probably have expended more energy, spoken more words, spent more time in thought and still more aspirin in the pursuit of faster starts in games. And yet they have finished every opening drive of every game -- including Thursday night -- with either a punt or a turnover (there were five punts and one interception in the season opener). And their Week 5 win against the Chargers was the only opening drive of a game to go even more than three plays.

articles.headline: Broncos beat the Seahawks 17-14 in OT on Ja'Quan McMillian's pick, Wil Lutz's 53-yarder
articles.description: — The Denver Broncos are atrocious on offense, depleted on defense and shaky on special teams. All they do is find ways to win.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコス、マクミリアンのインターセプトとルッツの53ヤードFGで、延長戦の末シアトルに17-14で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: デンバー・ブロンコスは、攻撃は壊滅的、守備は層が薄く、スペシャルチームも不安定だ。それでも、彼らは勝利する方法を見つけ続けている。
articles.body:
DENVER -- — The Denver Broncos are atrocious on offense, depleted on defense and shaky on special teams. All they do is find ways to win.


              Ja’Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold’s pass in overtime Thursday night and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal that gave the Broncos a 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks.


              The Broncos emerged from a tough six-week season-opening stretch with a 4-2 record despite an injury-riddled roster and a shaky quarterback, and the Seahawks (3-3) lost for the second time in five days. They also matched their loss total from last season, when they won their second Super Bowl title. 


              The Broncos won despite Bo Nix throwing for just 107 yards, J.K. Dobbins leading the rushing attack with a mere 41 yards and managing a meager three first downs and 168 yards of total offense — less than half the 353 yards piled up by the Seahawks.


              “I don't know why we can't really push the ball vertically right now,” Nix said. “But defenses are just sitting back and hanging out. ... Hopefully we find a way to get more out of it.”


              Nix was as honest as he's been to date in his postgame comments about Denver's scuffling offense.


              “We’re definitely capable, we’ve shown it," he said. "And, you know I don’t know where the disconnect is right now, to be honest with you. ... I just think we’re really, for some reason, struggling to find those explosive plays, and that’s what makes an offense really spectacular: Is finding explosive plays. And right now, we don’t have those.” 


              Denver's depleted defense came to the rescue yet again, hitting Darnold 17 times and collecting five sacks. 


              “The quarterback's getting hit way too much,” Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. “Everybody sees that.”


              “You’ve got to give credit to those guys," Darnold said. “They’ve got a really tough defense, really good defense coordinator in Vance (Joseph).”


              On Seattle's opening drive in overtime, McMillian intercepted a pass intended for Rashid Shaheed at the Denver 43, the second pick of the night by Darnold, who completed 27 of 51 passes for 278 yards without a touchdown.


              Those stats were better than Nix's. He barely topped 100 yards on 17-of-27 passing after throwing for 123 last week in a tight win over the Chargers.


              Jason Myers' 34-yard field goal tied it at 14-all with 3 seconds left in regulation and capped an 11-0 Seattle run over the final 5 1/2 minutes. The Seahawks started their game-tying drive at midfield after a 31-yard punt return by Shaheed.


              “No moral victories in the league,” Macdonald said. “It’s a bottom-line business, production business. But I’m proud of our effort. I’m proud of the resolve of the team. I’m proud of our connectedness of our team.

articles.descriptionJa: シアトル対デンバーの木曜夜の試合から、すべての主要プレーとハイライトをお届けします。
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Broncos (3-2) are hosting the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-2) on "Thursday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video).

Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle's slow start to the 2026 season is part of a bigger malaise for Denver's offense. The Broncos are 31st in the league in plays of 20 or more yards (with 11). Waddle is 65th in the league at 11.3 yards per catch and 69th in receiving yards per route run at 1.63, far below his 2.27 yards per route run last season with the Miami Dolphins. It's those types of figures that pushed coach Sean Payton to retake playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb after four games.

Seattle coordinator Brian Fleury's offense ranks eighth in scoring at 26.8 points per game. But it's also 25th in expected points added and 26th in ESPN's efficiency metric, indicative of flaws that Seattle's defense and special teams have helped cover. The Seahawks do lead the league in takaeaways with 11 and points off turnovers at 44.

Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold will bring you all the highlights and key plays from Thursday night, so be sure to check back in once the game kicks off.

articles.headline: Maxey: Healthy Embiid 'changes everything' for Sixers
articles.description: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.
articles.headlineJa: マクシー：「健康なエムビードがいれば、シックスターズのすべてが変わる」
articles.descriptionJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクシーは木曜日、ジョエル・エムビードが健康であることがシックスターズにとって「すべてを変える」と語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.

Embiid's 10-year career has been marred by injury. He has never played a full 82 games and has played more than 60 games just four times in his career. Over his 10 seasons, he has averaged just 49 games per season, which doesn't include him missing his first two seasons with injury.​

Embiid played just 38 games last season, double his number from 2024, as he navigated right hip complications, left knee management and appendicitis. The injuries have often kept Embiid out of training camp and the preseason -- crucial time for a team to get comfortable playing with a player like Embiid, the 2023 NBA MVP.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow."

Maxey said his experience gives him the advantage. He knows where Embiid likes to catch the ball, where he wants guards to cut and other tendencies that he has learned over six years of playing together. But many of the Sixers' new additions, most notably among them LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, don't have that luxury.

The difference this year is that they had a healthy Embiid in training camp and the preseason to make that transition easier.

​"If you haven't been playing with a big like Joel, there's not many. It's very hard, very difficult to learn certain things," he said. "...So, with him being here, we can drill those things over and over. It's been what, like two, three weeks that we've had just drilling and drilling. That's a good thing."

At the end of last season, Embiid said he was "as confident as I've ever been" about his health moving forward.

"I think, obviously, [my knee] was the biggest concern, and I'm not thinking about it," he said. "And as long as we keep doing what we've been doing, I won't have to think about it anymore.

Some other big takeaways? Derrick White was picked at the end of Round 2. Stephen Curry fell to pick No. 32. And only four rookies were drafted.
